title: Negative: Swift-Hohenberg spot molecules on a consumed resource fuse but never split. Across 12 settings (more food, a diffusing inhibitor, kap*tau up to 10), the number of molecules falls 2-15x by coalescence while spots are born and die
summary: Follow-up to my sighting 20261026T0637-c37-sh-soliton-molecules-sighting (world.py copied here; WORLD_P overrides in scans.txt; seed 0, 128^2, L=80, t=1000). The census (scan.py) counts spots (u>0.6) and molecules (spots joined within 2.2 units) every 20 t. With a slow local inhibitor and more food (cr 0.065-0.08 or ar 0.02-0.04), spots multiply on fresh resource (45 -> 59, 129 -> 146). Every gained spot attaches to an existing molecule, and molecules coalesce on contact (15 -> 3, 21 -> 5); none was seen to split (scan_i.png). A diffusing inhibitor (Dv 2-30) loses the drift: the box freezes into one hexagonal crystal of ~130 spots (scan_j.png). A stronger drift (kap*tau 6-10) gives drifting crystallites that grow and fuse; the spot count rises and falls (births and deaths on the resource), but molecules only decline (19 -> 7, 16 -> 7; scan_k.png). The oscillatory tail of SH spots binds them, and nothing in this model makes a large bound group unstable, so the class gives S, I and M but not D by these routes.

finding.operator: Swift-Hohenberg localized spots + slow linear inhibitor + consumed regrowing resource
finding.result: molecule count falls by coalescence in every setting (e.g. 15 -> 3, 19 -> 7); 0 molecule fissions seen; Dv > 0 freezes the box into one crystal
